input.title: The Adyghe School in Syria
input.notes: The Adyghe Private School was established in Qunaitra, Syria, in 1932 and continued operating until 1942. It was the first Circassian elementary school in the diaspora where the entire curriculum was taught in the Circassian language, except for Arabic language classes.

examples.description: A 20th-century photograph from Qunaitra, Syria showing the Adyghe School. The school was established in 1932 and continued operating until 1942. It was the first Circassian elementary school in the diaspora where the entire curriculum was taught in the Circassian language except for Arabic language classes.

input.title: A meeting under a tree
input.keywords: Tree, tree veneration, under tree gathering
input.notes: It was a tradition among Circassian people to hold their gatherings, meetings, and rituals under trees. Each village or town would have a specific tree designated for such gatherings.

examples.description: A painting showing a meeting under a tree. It was a tradition among Circassian people to hold their gatherings, meetings, and rituals under trees.

input.title: Dautoqua Zaurbek (Serebriakov)
input.notes: Fought in WW1 and returned home as a commander, and became the organizer of the anti-Bolshevik movement in Kabarda in 1918. He was the assistant to Prince Tembot Zhankhotovich. and he announced the creation of the "Free Kabarda" party.

context.other: Photo Session, "Free Kabarda" Party, Bolshevik Revolution

examples.description: Datouqua Zaurbek (1886-1919), fought in WW1 and returned home as a commander, and became the organizer of the anti-Bolshevik movement in Kabarda in 1918.
